7. Mr. S.N. Goswami, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that Section 14 of the Limitation Act, shall apply in special law unless excluded expressly. He also submits that the petitioner wrongly preferred Criminal Revision against the order of Tribunal and as such he is entitled to get benefit of Section 14 of the Limitation Act. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate referred to the case of Abdul Wahab Sheikh Vs. Md. Kamal Hossain alias Md. Kalam Hossain & Others reported in 20 BLT (AD) 282; the case of Mohammad Salim and others Vs. Syedul Haque Chowdhury and others reported in 10 MLR (AD) 65 and the case of Abul Bashar Vs. Investment Corporation of Bangladesh and another reported in 52 DLR(AD) 178. 

 9. There is no doubt that the proceedings of Criminal Revision against the order of Tribunal initiated and continued in a wrong forum, the time spent in prosecuting the same with due diligence in the wrong forum shall be excluded from the period of limitation as provided under Section 14 of the Limitation Act. But our concern is whether this petitioner will get benefit of Section 5 of the Limitation Act. The petitioner preferred Criminal Revision No.1283 of 2012 against the order dated 31.05.2012 passed by the Tribunal. Said Criminal Revision was rejected vide judgment and order dated 14.10.2012. Obviously, this period shall be excluded under Section 14 of the Limitation Act. But admittedly the petitioner filed application for certified copy of the judgment and order on 15.11.2012 i.e. almost one month after delivery of the judgment and order in Criminal Revision No.1283 of 2012. It is to be mentioned here that the petitioner filed application under Section 5 read with Section 14 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in preferring the Criminal Appeal and Rule was issued on that application. 

 10. Section 29(2)(a) of the Limitation Act, runs as follows : 

 11. It is not disputed that Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, is a special law. It cannot also be disputed that if this Ain prescribed limitation for filing any suit, appeal or application, a period of limitation different from the period prescribed by this AM would be inapplicable, unless the special law makes it applicable. 

 "We make it clear again that the provisions contained in sections 4, 9-18 and 22 of the Limitation Act are applicable in determining the period of limitation prescribed by any special law for filing any suit, appeal or application where such special law does not expressly exclude the applicability of the provisions of these sections of the Limitation Act. The remaining provisions of the Limitation Act shall not apply in any proceeding under any special law. (See Clause (b) of Sub-Section (2) of Section 29 of the Limitation Act.)" 

 14. From the above discussions it is clear that Section 5 is not applicable in any proceeding under any special law as provided under Section 29(2)(b) of the Limitation Act.
